summary.title: HireHub Recruitment Portal - Threat Model
summary.description: Prelim Exam - Threat Modeling Practical. Scenario 6: HireHub Recruitment Portal. Applicants submit applications and upload resumes; recruiters review candidates and initiate background checks via a third-party vendor API.

threats.title: Applicant identity spoofing
threats.description: An attacker uses stolen, guessed, or credential-stuffed login details (or a hijacked session token) to impersonate a legitimate applicant, submit fraudulent applications, or view/modify that applicant's profile and uploaded resume.
threats.mitigation: Enforce MFA for applicant accounts, rate-limit and monitor login attempts, use short-lived rotating session tokens, and bind sessions to device/IP fingerprint where feasible.

threats.title: Applicant action repudiation
threats.description: An applicant denies having submitted a specific application, withdrawn an application, or uploaded a specific resume version, and the portal cannot produce sufficient evidence (timestamped, attributable logs) to refute the claim.
threats.mitigation: Log every applicant-initiated action (submit, edit, withdraw, upload) with timestamp, authenticated user ID, and source IP; retain immutable audit logs.

threats.title: Recruiter identity spoofing
threats.description: An attacker phishes or otherwise obtains a recruiter's credentials (or hijacks a recruiter session) to gain access to the candidate review dashboard, applicant PII, and the ability to initiate background checks.
threats.mitigation: Enforce MFA and SSO for recruiter accounts, enforce short session timeouts, and alert on logins from new devices/locations.

threats.title: Recruiter action repudiation
threats.description: A recruiter denies having reviewed, rejected, or initiated a background check on a specific candidate, and there is no reliable, attributable audit trail to establish who performed the action and when.
threats.mitigation: Log all recruiter actions (candidate review, status changes, background-check initiation) with authenticated user ID and timestamp in a tamper-evident audit log used for compliance review.

threats.title: Vendor API endpoint spoofing
threats.description: An attacker stands up a rogue endpoint, performs DNS hijacking, or downgrades TLS to impersonate the legitimate Background Check Vendor API and harvest applicant PII sent for screening.
threats.mitigation: Pin the vendor's TLS certificate/public key, validate the full certificate chain, and use mutual TLS or signed API requests for the vendor integration.

threats.title: Vendor request/response repudiation
threats.description: The vendor disputes having received a specific background-check request, or the portal disputes the results the vendor claims to have returned, with no non-repudiable record (e.g., signed requests/responses, correlation IDs) on either side.
threats.mitigation: Require signed requests and responses with correlation/transaction IDs, and retain both sides' signed payloads for the compliance retention period.

threats.title: Credential stuffing / brute force login
threats.description: An attacker automates login attempts against the Authenticate User process using leaked credential lists or brute force, potentially gaining access as an applicant or recruiter.
threats.mitigation: Enforce account lockout/backoff, CAPTCHA after repeated failures, MFA, and monitor for credential-stuffing patterns.

threats.title: Session/token tampering for privilege escalation
threats.description: An attacker modifies an authentication token or session cookie (e.g., a JWT role claim) to change their assigned role from applicant to recruiter.
threats.mitigation: Use signed, server-validated tokens (e.g., JWT with strong signature verification), never trust client-supplied role claims, and re-derive role from server-side state.

threats.title: Insufficient authentication event logging
threats.description: Login successes, failures, and password changes are not logged with enough detail (timestamp, source IP, user agent, outcome) to reconstruct an account-takeover incident after the fact.
threats.mitigation: Centrally log all authentication events with timestamp, source IP, and outcome; alert on anomalous patterns.

threats.title: Account enumeration via verbose auth errors
threats.description: Distinct error messages for 'user not found' versus 'wrong password' (or password-reset flows) let an attacker enumerate valid applicant and recruiter email addresses.
threats.mitigation: Return generic authentication error messages and use consistent response timing regardless of whether the account exists.

threats.title: Login endpoint flooding
threats.description: An attacker floods the Authenticate User process with high-volume login requests, exhausting compute resources or triggering mass account lockouts that deny access to legitimate applicants and recruiters.
threats.mitigation: Apply rate limiting and IP/device reputation checks at the edge (WAF/API gateway), and use progressive lockout that cannot be weaponized to lock out arbitrary users.

threats.title: Role manipulation for privilege escalation
threats.description: A flaw in role assignment logic allows an authenticated applicant to obtain a recruiter session or elevated privileges by manipulating a client-supplied role or scope parameter.
threats.mitigation: Assign and enforce roles exclusively from server-side, authoritative data; never accept role/permission values from the client.

threats.title: Forged applicant identity on submission
threats.description: An attacker submits an application under a forged or unverified applicant identity (e.g., using someone else's name/email without verification) to plant fraudulent data in the system.
threats.mitigation: Require verified email/identity confirmation before an application is accepted, and bind submissions to an authenticated session.

threats.title: Parameter tampering on application submission
threats.description: An attacker manipulates hidden form fields or API parameters (e.g., applicant ID, job posting ID) to submit an application on behalf of another applicant or against a job posting not shown to them.
threats.mitigation: Validate that the authenticated session owns the applicant ID and that the job posting ID is active/visible server-side; never trust client-supplied ownership fields.

threats.title: Unverifiable application content
threats.description: There is no immutable, timestamped, hashed record of exactly what content an applicant submitted, so an applicant can later dispute what was in their application.
threats.mitigation: Store a cryptographic hash and timestamp of each submitted application payload in an append-only audit log.

threats.title: IDOR exposes other applicants' submissions
threats.description: An insecure direct object reference on the submission/edit endpoint allows an attacker to view or edit another applicant's in-progress or submitted application by changing an ID parameter.
threats.mitigation: Enforce server-side authorization checks that the authenticated user owns the application record on every read/write.

threats.title: Automated bulk/bot application flooding
threats.description: An attacker scripts a large volume of automated application submissions, exhausting database and storage capacity and degrading the service for legitimate applicants.
threats.mitigation: Add CAPTCHA/bot detection on the submission endpoint, rate-limit per account/IP, and monitor submission volume anomalies.

threats.title: Mass assignment to privileged fields
threats.description: A mass-assignment flaw lets an applicant set fields in the submission payload that should be recruiter-only (e.g., application status, internal notes, 'shortlisted' flag).
threats.mitigation: Use an explicit allow-list of applicant-writable fields server-side; reject or ignore any other fields in the request.

threats.title: Resume upload under a spoofed session
threats.description: An attacker exploits a session-fixation or CSRF flaw to upload a resume while impersonating another applicant's session, attaching unwanted or malicious content to that applicant's profile.
threats.mitigation: Use anti-CSRF tokens, SameSite cookies, and re-validate session ownership on the upload endpoint.

threats.title: Malicious file uploaded as a resume
threats.description: An attacker uploads a file disguised as a resume (e.g., a macro-laden document, embedded script, or polyglot file) that executes malicious code when opened by a recruiter or processed by an automated resume parser.
threats.mitigation: Restrict accepted file types/extensions, strip active content, scan uploads with antivirus/sandboxing, and render resumes in a safe viewer rather than opening the native file.

threats.title: No integrity record for uploaded files
threats.description: There is no hash or logged linkage tying a specific uploaded file to a specific applicant session and timestamp, making it impossible to prove which file was uploaded and when.
threats.mitigation: Compute and store a content hash plus authenticated uploader ID and timestamp for every uploaded file.

threats.title: Predictable resume storage paths
threats.description: Predictable or unauthenticated storage URLs/paths allow an attacker to enumerate and directly download other applicants' resumes from Document Storage, bypassing the application.
threats.mitigation: Use non-guessable object keys, require authenticated/authorized signed URLs with short expiry for all resume access.

threats.title: Storage exhaustion via oversized/flooded uploads
threats.description: An attacker uploads oversized files or floods the upload endpoint with requests, exhausting Document Storage capacity or upload bandwidth and blocking legitimate applicants from uploading.
threats.mitigation: Enforce file size limits, per-account upload quotas/rate limits, and storage capacity alerts.

threats.title: Code execution via resume parser vulnerability
threats.description: An attacker crafts a resume file that exploits a vulnerability in a downstream resume-parsing library, achieving code execution with the application process's privileges.
threats.mitigation: Run file parsing in an isolated/sandboxed worker with minimal privileges, keep parsing libraries patched, and validate file structure before parsing.

threats.title: Recruiter session spoofing for bulk access
threats.description: An attacker impersonates a recruiter session to browse, filter, and export the full applicant database beyond what any single recruiter should access.
threats.mitigation: Bind sessions to device fingerprint, require MFA, and set per-session/per-account export limits with alerting.

threats.title: Unauthorized tampering with candidate status
threats.description: A malicious or compromised recruiter account silently changes a candidate's status, notes, or ranking (e.g., rejecting a candidate) without proper authorization or a visible trail.
threats.mitigation: Require role-appropriate approval for status changes on shortlisted/offer-stage candidates and record before/after values in an audit log.

threats.title: Untraceable candidate review decisions
threats.description: Recruiter actions in the review process (viewing, shortlisting, rejecting) are not logged per authenticated user, making it impossible to trace which recruiter made which hiring-related decision.
threats.mitigation: Log every review action with recruiter ID, candidate ID, action, and timestamp in an audit trail retained per HR record-keeping requirements.

threats.title: Over-exposure of sensitive applicant fields
threats.description: Lack of field-level access control exposes sensitive applicant data (e.g., identifiers, protected characteristics collected for EEO purposes) to recruiters who should not see them, or to recruiters outside the relevant business unit.
threats.mitigation: Apply field-level and record-level access control based on recruiter role/department; mask protected-characteristic fields from hiring decision-makers where required.

threats.title: Expensive search queries degrade availability
threats.description: Unbounded or unindexed search/filter queries issued from the review UI allow an attacker (or a careless recruiter) to trigger expensive database scans that degrade the Applicant Profiles DB for all users.
threats.mitigation: Add query timeouts, pagination limits, and proper indexing; rate-limit search requests per recruiter.

threats.title: Privilege escalation to admin-only actions
threats.description: A recruiter exploits an authorization gap to reach admin-only functionality from the review interface, such as bulk-exporting all candidates or editing job postings they should not manage.
threats.mitigation: Enforce server-side role checks on every admin action, independent of what the UI displays, and log attempted access to out-of-scope functions.

threats.title: Spoofed or replayed vendor request
threats.description: An attacker spoofs or replays a captured request to the Background Check Vendor API to trigger unauthorized background checks or to retrieve results for a candidate they should not have access to.
threats.mitigation: Use mutual TLS or signed, nonce-based requests with short validity windows to the vendor API; reject replayed requests.

threats.title: Tampered vendor request payload
threats.description: An attacker intercepts and modifies the payload sent to the Background Check Vendor API (e.g., swapping the candidate identifier), causing results to be misapplied to the wrong applicant.
threats.mitigation: Use TLS with certificate pinning and integrity-protected (signed/HMAC'd) payloads for all vendor requests.

threats.title: No auditable link between recruiter and check request
threats.description: There is no signed or reliably logged record correlating which recruiter initiated which background-check request and when, complicating compliance audits (e.g., FCRA adverse-action requirements).
threats.mitigation: Log recruiter ID, candidate ID, consent record reference, and vendor transaction/correlation ID for every initiated check, retained per compliance policy.

threats.title: PII exposure to/from the vendor
threats.description: Applicant PII (e.g., full name, DOB, SSN-equivalent identifiers, address) sent to the vendor is exposed via an unencrypted channel, overly verbose application logs, or an overscoped/leaked vendor API key.
threats.mitigation: Encrypt PII in transit and avoid logging raw PII; scope the vendor API key to minimum required permissions and rotate it regularly.

threats.title: Background-check request flooding
threats.description: An attacker (or a scripting error) triggers a large volume of background-check initiations, exhausting the vendor's rate limit, incurring excessive cost, or disrupting the integration for legitimate use.
threats.mitigation: Rate-limit background-check initiation per recruiter/account and require explicit, logged approval before each request is sent.

threats.title: Unauthorized triggering of background checks
threats.description: A flaw in the integration allows an unauthorized actor (e.g., an applicant, or a recruiter without the required approval level) to trigger a background check without proper recruiter authorization and applicant consent verification.
threats.mitigation: Enforce server-side authorization and a verified-consent precondition before any request reaches the vendor API; restrict the initiation action to authorized recruiter roles only.

threats.title: Unauthorized modification of applicant records
threats.description: An attacker who gains database access (e.g., via a SQL injection flaw in Submit Application or Review Candidates) modifies applicant profile fields, such as changing an application status to 'hired' or altering contact details.
threats.mitigation: Use parameterized queries/ORM everywhere, apply least-privilege DB accounts per service, and enable change-tracking on sensitive fields.

threats.title: Bulk PII exposure from the profiles database
threats.description: Misconfigured database permissions, a missing access control check, or a SQL injection flaw exposes the full Applicant Profiles DB, leaking PII for all applicants at once.
threats.mitigation: Encrypt PII at rest, apply least-privilege network and IAM access to the database, and monitor for anomalous bulk-read query patterns.

threats.title: Query-based resource exhaustion
threats.description: An attacker (or an unoptimized recruiter search) performs resource-intensive, unindexed queries against the Applicant Profiles DB, degrading availability for the entire portal.
threats.mitigation: Add indexing on commonly filtered fields, enforce query timeouts and result-size limits, and isolate heavy read workloads from transactional workloads.

threats.title: Unauthorized edits to job postings
threats.description: An attacker with write access alters job posting content (e.g., salary, requirements) to mislead applicants, or inserts malicious content (stored XSS) into a posting description.
threats.mitigation: Restrict job-posting write access to authorized recruiter/admin roles, sanitize and encode posting content, and log all edits.

threats.title: Exposure of internal-only job postings
threats.description: Draft or internal-only postings (e.g., unannounced roles or internal salary bands) are exposed to unauthorized applicants due to missing visibility/access controls on the Job Postings DB.
threats.mitigation: Enforce a publish-state check on every read path so only 'published' postings are visible externally.

threats.title: Search endpoint overload against job listings
threats.description: An attacker floods job-search/listing endpoints with expensive queries against the Job Postings DB, degrading availability for applicants browsing openings.
threats.mitigation: Cache published listings, rate-limit search requests, and add query timeouts/indexing.

threats.title: Resume file replacement
threats.description: An attacker with access to Document Storage replaces a legitimate applicant's resume with a malicious or defamatory document, affecting that applicant's candidacy.
threats.mitigation: Enforce write-once/versioned storage with integrity hashes, and restrict write access to the Upload Resume process only.

threats.title: Unauthenticated access to stored resumes
threats.description: An overly permissive storage bucket or ACL configuration allows direct, unauthenticated access to uploaded resumes containing PII, bypassing the portal's access controls entirely.
threats.mitigation: Keep the storage bucket private, require short-lived signed URLs for every access, and audit bucket policy regularly.

threats.title: Storage capacity exhaustion
threats.description: An attacker uploads a large volume of oversized files, exhausting Document Storage quota or throughput and blocking new resume uploads for legitimate applicants.
threats.mitigation: Enforce per-file size limits, per-account quotas, and automated capacity alerting/scaling.

threats.title: Credential interception in transit
threats.description: Login credentials sent from the Applicant's browser over the internet to the portal could be intercepted via a man-in-the-middle attack if TLS is missing or misconfigured.
threats.mitigation: Enforce HTTPS/TLS 1.2+ for all traffic, use HSTS, and disable plaintext HTTP entirely.

threats.title: PII exposure to third-party vendor in transit
threats.description: Applicant PII and consent data sent to the Background Check Vendor API could be intercepted or logged insecurely if the connection is not strongly encrypted and certificate-validated.
threats.mitigation: Use TLS 1.2+ with certificate pinning to the vendor endpoint, and avoid logging raw PII in application/API logs.

threats.title: Tampering with returned results in transit
threats.description: Background check results returned by the vendor could be tampered with in transit, causing the portal to act on incorrect information for a hiring decision.
threats.mitigation: Require signed/HMAC'd vendor responses and verify the signature before accepting results.
